newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Foncier H2 could be like H1.
newsitem.headline: Credit Foncier H2 could be like H1.

text.p: Credit Foncier said on Wednesday that the second half of the year could be in line with the first half result, barring any new products and exceptional charges and depending on a year-end property risk assessment.

The property lending group, which is in the intitial stages of being wound down under a government plan since a huge 1995 loss, posted a net attributable profit of 402 million francs in the first half.

"The expected result for the second half of 1996 could be in line with that of the first half, but depending on the property risk analysis at the end of the year and barring new products and exceptional charges," the group said in a statement.

"Net banking income should be better than expected in forecasts given the bigger than expected fall in short term rates," it added, adding that general operating costs should fall by about eight percent compared to 1995," it said.
The overall risk charge should also be less significant than expected, it said.

It said loan production was expected to fall 50 percent to 16.5 billion francs for the year versus 36.3 billion francs in 1995, after an 87 percent fall in the area of PAP low-cost housing loans, where Credit Foncier's monopoly was abolished in October 1995.
Credit Foncier said it expected a 70 percent drop in credits to local authorities and a rise of around 40 percent in housing credits to 9.5 billion francs from 6.9 billion francs.
